title: COEP reporting for workers expects an environment settings object but gets Document or WorkerGlobalScope objects
body:
See https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#worker-processing-model 

step 2:

> Let _owner_ be the [relevant owner to add](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#relevant-owner-to-add) given _outside settings_.


> Given an [environment settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#environment-settings-object) _o_ when creating or obtaining a worker, the **relevant owner to add** depends on the type of [global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-settings-object-global) specified by _o_. If _o_ specifies a global object that is a `WorkerGlobalScope` object (i.e., if we are creating a nested dedicated worker), then the relevant owner is that global object. Otherwise, _o_ specifies a [global object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-settings-object-global) that is a `Window` object, and the relevant owner is the [responsible document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#responsible-document) specified by _o_.

So _owner_ is either a `WorkerGlobalScope` object or a `Document` object.

step 14.8:

> If the result of [checking a global object's embedder policy](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#check-a-global-object's-embedder-policy) with _worker global scope_, _owner_, and _response_ is false, then set _response_ to a network error.

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#check-a-global-object's-embedder-policy says

> To **check a global object's embedder policy** given a `WorkerGlobalScope` _workerGlobalScope_, an [environment settings object](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#environment-settings-object) _owner_, and a [response](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-response) _response_:

_owner_ is expected to be an environment settings object, but it will be either a `Document` object or a `WorkerGlobalScope` object.

Should "run a worker" pass _outside settings_ instead of _owner_?
